question:
Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.
The boys and the teacher wants to win.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. want to win.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The subject "The boys and the teacher" consists of two different persons/entities joined by "and", so it takes a plural verb — "want", not the singular "wants".

• Rule — Subject-Verb Agreement: When two or more different subjects are joined by "and", the verb used with them must be plural, unless the subjects together refer to a single person/idea.

• Also, after "want" the following verb must be in its base form (infinitive with "to") — "to win", not "to won" (won is the past tense/past participle of "win" and cannot follow "to").
◦ Correct: The boys and the teacher want to win.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "wants to won" is incorrect on two counts — the singular verb "wants" does not agree with the plural compound subject, and "to won" is an invalid infinitive form.

• Option 2: "want to won" correctly uses the plural verb "want" but wrongly uses "to won" instead of "to win".

• Option 3: "want win" drops the infinitive marker "to" that must precede the base verb "win" here.

NOTE

• Remember: subjects joined by "and" normally take a plural verb, e.g., "Ram and Shyam are friends." Exceptions occur when the two nouns denote a single entity/idea (e.g., "Bread and butter is my breakfast.").

• After want/wish/hope/decide etc., use "to" + base verb (V1), never the past form.

question:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the underlined word.
He was compelled by everyone to join the group.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Induced.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The word "Compelled" means forced or obliged to do something, often against one's will. (जबरदस्ती करना/मजबूर करना)

• Its antonym is "Induced", which means persuaded or led to do something willingly, through gentle influence or incentive, rather than force. (प्रेरित करना/मनाना)
◦ Example: No one compelled her to resign; she was simply induced by a better job offer.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1: Demur (आपत्ति करना): To raise objections or show reluctance; it is unrelated in meaning to "compelled" and its opposite.

• Option 2: Obscured (अस्पष्ट करना): To make something unclear or hidden from view; not connected to force/persuasion.

• Option 3: Confessed (स्वीकार करना): To admit something, usually a fault or crime; not an antonym of "compelled".

NOTE

• Other synonyms of "compelled": forced, coerced, obliged, pressured.

• Other words meaning "induced/persuaded": coaxed, prevailed upon, cajoled, talked into.

question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.
To kick the bucket
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. To die.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom "To kick the bucket" means to die, and is used informally, often with a hint of dark humour. (मर जाना)
◦ Example: The old man finally kicked the bucket at the age of ninety-five.

• The idiom is believed to originate from the way an animal being slaughtered would kick against the bucket/beam it was suspended from, or from a person standing on a bucket to hang themselves kicking it away.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1: To be ill is the meaning of idioms like "Under the weather", not "kick the bucket".

• Option 2: Be sad is closer to idioms like "Down in the dumps" or "Feeling blue".

• Option 3: Be happy is the meaning of idioms like "On cloud nine" or "Over the moon", the opposite sense.

NOTE

• Other idioms/euphemisms related to death often asked in SSC: "Breathe one's last", "Pass away", "Give up the ghost", "Meet one's maker".

question:
Identify and correct the INCORRECTLY spelt word in the given sentence.
The Collector paid floral tributes to the statue of Mahatma Gandhi after hosting the flag.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. hoisting.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In the given sentence, the word "hosting" is used incorrectly; the correct word required by the context (raising a flag) is "hoisting".

• "Hoist" means to raise or lift up, especially a flag, whereas "host" means to organise an event or to be a person who receives guests.
◦ Example: The soldiers stood at attention while hoisting the national flag.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "floaral" is an incorrect spelling; the correctly spelt word already present in the sentence is "floral", not "floaral".

• Option 2: "stateu" is an incorrect spelling of "statue", which is already spelt correctly in the given sentence.

• Option 3: "trebutes" is an incorrect spelling of "tributes", which is already spelt correctly in the given sentence.

NOTE

• Commonly confused pairs in SSC spelling questions: hoist/host, statue/statute, stationary/stationery, complement/compliment.

• Always read the full sentence for meaning before checking spellings — a word may be spelt correctly but be the wrong word for the context (like "hosting" here, which is a real but contextually wrong word).

question:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the underlined word.
Do you know the old adage 'the show must go on'?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Misconstruction.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The word "Adage" means a traditional saying that is widely accepted as embodying a general truth or piece of wisdom. (प्रचलित सूक्ति/कहावत, जो सामान्यतः सत्य मानी जाती है)

• Its antonym is "Misconstruction", which means a wrong or false interpretation/understanding of something, the opposite of an accepted, well-understood truth. (गलत व्याख्या/भ्रांति)
◦ Example: His careless remark was open to misconstruction by the press.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2: Rebuke (डांटना): A sharp criticism or reprimand; unrelated to the sense of "an accepted saying".

• Option 3: Dare (चुनौती देना): A challenge to do something risky; not connected in meaning to "adage".

• Option 4: Addiction (लत): A compulsive dependence on something; unrelated to the meaning of "adage".

NOTE

• Other words close in meaning to "adage": proverb, maxim, saying, aphorism, axiom.

• "Misconstruction/misconstrue" is a frequently tested antonym-pair word in SSC exams for words expressing "an established/accepted truth".

question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.
She reminds me always that I ________ to be a little more careful.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. have.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The sentence requires the structure "have to", which expresses an obligation or necessity in the Present tense — "I have to be a little more careful" means "it is necessary for me to be a little more careful".

• Rule — Subject-Verb Agreement with "have to": With the subject "I", the correct auxiliary is "have"; "has" is used only with third person singular subjects (he/she/it/singular noun).
◦ Correct: I have to go. / He has to go.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "had" would give the Past tense meaning ("I had to be careful" — that I once needed to be), which does not fit the Present-tense reminding action ("reminds me always").

• Option 3: "must" cannot correctly combine with a following "to" in this structure — "must" is a modal verb and is never followed by "to" (i.e. "must to be" is grammatically wrong).

• Option 4: "has" does not agree with the first-person singular subject "I"; it would only be correct with he/she/it.

NOTE

• "Have to"/"has to"/"had to" express external obligation, while "must" expresses the speaker's own/internal obligation and is never followed by "to".

• Since the main clause verb "reminds" is in the Present tense, the reported/that-clause here also stays in the Present tense ("have to").

question:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the word given in brackets to fill in the blank.
Mr. Khanna is quite ___________(callous) towards the victims of earthquake.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. sympathetic.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The word "Callous" means showing or feeling no emotion, sympathy, or concern for others; hard-hearted and insensitive. (निर्दयी/संवेदनहीन)

• Its antonym is "Sympathetic", meaning feeling or showing kindness, understanding, and concern for someone's suffering. (सहानुभूतिपूर्ण)
◦ Example: Unlike his callous colleague, Mr. Khanna is quite sympathetic towards the victims of the earthquake.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "rationalistic" relates to reasoning based on logic, not on emotion/kindness; it is not the opposite of "callous".

• Option 2: "unsympathetic" is actually a synonym, not an antonym, of "callous" — both describe a lack of sympathy.

• Option 4: "nondiplomatic" relates to a lack of tact in dealing with people, not to (in)sensitivity towards suffering; it does not oppose "callous" in the required sense.

NOTE

• Other synonyms of "callous": insensitive, unfeeling, heartless, indifferent.

• Other antonyms of "callous": compassionate, considerate, tender-hearted, warm-hearted.

question:
Sentences of a paragraph are given below. While the first and the last sentences (S1 and S6) are in the correct order, the sentences in between are jumbled up and named P, Q, R, S. Arrange the sentences in the correct order to form a meaningful and coherent paragraph.

(S1) Newspapers, especially of the popular variety, aim to do two things: to inform and to entertain.
(P) Entertainment may be principally found in the centre pages of the newspaper in some of the feature articles and in some local news stories.
(Q) The principal aim of the short news report on the front pages is to inform.
(R) Most newspapers are published daily, and the news reporters must make sure that they have up-to-the-minute news.
(S) In their news reports they will aim to create a sense of immediacy, to convey the impression that they have 'rushed' the news to the reader and 'that the information contained is the very latest.'
(S6) Reporters also wish to create a sense of authenticity, that is, that their news is accurate and genuine.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. P, Q, R, S.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• S1 states that newspapers aim to do two things: to inform and to entertain. The paragraph must first take up these two purposes, and then move to a related, connected idea before reaching S6.

• P naturally follows S1 by first locating entertainment ("Entertainment may be principally found in the centre pages…"), and Q follows by locating information ("The principal aim of the short news report on the front pages is to inform.") — together P and Q expand on the two aims named in S1.

• R then shifts to how newspapers achieve up-to-date informing — "Most newspapers are published daily, and the news reporters must make sure that they have up-to-the-minute news" — which logically follows from Q's idea of "informing".

• S follows R by explaining the effect of this up-to-the-minute reporting — creating "a sense of immediacy" — which then leads smoothly into S6, where reporters "also" wish to create "a sense of authenticity", building on the "sense of immediacy" idea of S.
◦ Final order: S1 → P → Q → R → S → S6.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 (Q, S, R, P) is incorrect because it places S (about immediacy, which depends on R's idea of daily publishing) before R, breaking the cause-effect link.

• Option 2 (R, P, S, Q) is incorrect because it starts with R (about daily publishing) before the two aims of the paper — inform/entertain — introduced in S1 have even been picked up by P and Q.

• Option 3 (S, R, P, Q) is incorrect because it places S (which depends on R for context) before R, and separates P and Q from immediately following S1.

NOTE

• In para-jumble questions, always check which sentence directly continues the idea/keyword of S1 (or S6) — here, the two aims "inform" and "entertain" in S1 are the linking keywords for P and Q.

• Pronouns and linking words like "also", "that", "their" are strong clues — S6's "also wish to create a sense of…" directly echoes S's "aim to create a sense of immediacy".

question:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word from the sentence.
Ready
She was preparing dinner in an organised manner using well-equipped tools while listening to the radio.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Preparing.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The word "Ready" means prepared and available for use or action. (तैयार)

• Among the given options, "Preparing" is closest in meaning to "ready/prepared", since to prepare something is to make it ready.
◦ Example: She was preparing (getting ready) the report before the meeting.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2: "Listening" means paying attention to sound; it has no meaning-relationship with "ready".

• Option 3: "Organised" means arranged in a systematic way; it describes order/method, not the state of being ready.

• Option 4: "Equipped" means supplied with the necessary items/tools for a purpose; it is related to having resources, not directly to the sense of "ready".

NOTE

• Other synonyms of "ready": prepared, set, primed, geared up.

• In such "synonym from the sentence" questions, always match the core dictionary meaning of the given word to the closest word/phrase in the passage, rather than picking a word merely because it appears prominent in the sentence.

question: Identify how you will ask everyone if the children were not reading the books in passive voice.
option_1: Were the books being read by the children?
option_2: Were the books not being read by the children?
option_3: Were the book not being read by the children?
option_4: Were the children reading the books?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Were the books not being read by the children?

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The sentence to be converted is an interrogative negative sentence in the Past Continuous Tense: "Were the children not reading the books?"

• Rule — Passive Voice of Interrogative (Yes/No question) sentences in Past Continuous Tense:
◦ Active: Was/Were + Subject + not + V1-ing + Object?
◦ Passive: Was/Were + Object + not + being + V3 + by + Subject?

• Applying the rule: the object "the books" (plural) becomes the subject, so the auxiliary is "Were"; the negative "not" stays in the same position; "reading" becomes "being read" (V3 of read = read); and "the children" becomes the agent with "by".
◦ Passive: Were the books not being read by the children?

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 is incorrect because it drops the "not", changing a negative question into an affirmative one and altering the meaning.

• Option 3 is incorrect because it wrongly uses the singular "book" instead of the plural "books", and also drops "not".

• Option 4 is incorrect because it is framed in the active voice ("were the children reading"), not the passive voice asked for.

NOTE

• In passive interrogative sentences, the auxiliary verb (was/were/is/are) moves to the very front, but "not" (in a negative question) stays immediately after the new subject.

• The past participle (V3) of "read" is spelt the same as V1 ("read"), but is pronounced differently ("red" instead of "reed").

question:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word.
Hostile
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Unfriendly.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The word "Hostile" means unfriendly, antagonistic, or opposed in attitude. (शत्रुतापूर्ण/विरोधी)

• Its closest synonym among the options is "Unfriendly", which conveys the same sense of a lack of warmth or goodwill towards someone.
◦ Example: The villagers gave the strangers a hostile (unfriendly) reception.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "Pleasant" means agreeable or enjoyable; it is actually an antonym, not a synonym, of "hostile".

• Option 2: "Hospitable" means welcoming and generous towards guests; it is also an antonym of "hostile".

• Option 3: "Empathetic" means being able to understand and share the feelings of others; it is unrelated to, and roughly opposite in spirit to, "hostile".

NOTE

• Other synonyms of "hostile": antagonistic, belligerent, aggressive, adversarial, inimical.

• Other antonyms of "hostile": friendly, amicable, cordial, welcoming.

question:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.
The fact that God created man in his personal view by giving him an intellectual spirit elevates him above the beasts of the field.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. own image.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The correct, idiomatically fixed expression is "in his own image", meaning made to resemble oneself in form or likeness. (अपने ही स्वरूप/प्रतिरूप में)

• This is a well-known set phrase (drawn from the idea that "God created man in His own image") used to describe someone creating another being or thing resembling themselves.
◦ Example: The sculptor liked to think that he had shaped the statue in his own image.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "own glory" refers to one's own honour or splendour, not to resemblance/likeness, so it does not fit the intended meaning.

• Option 2: "own capacity" refers to one's own ability or capability, unrelated to the idea of being made in someone's likeness.

• Option 4: "own idea" refers to a personal thought or notion, not to physical/spiritual resemblance, so it does not convey the intended sense.

NOTE

• The fixed phrase "in someone's own image" is frequently tested — remember it always pairs with "image", not with synonyms like "view", "idea" or "capacity".

• Similar fixed expressions tested in SSC: "in one's own right", "in the same vein", "in due course".

question:
Sentences of a paragraph are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the sentences in the correct order to form a meaningful and coherent paragraph.

(A) During the summer, I noticed that the leaves of the tree were beginning to wither.
(B) I am especially proud of it, not only because it has survived several winters, but because it occasionally produces luscious peaches.
(C) The tree had grown against a warm wall on a sheltered side of the house.
(D) Last summer, I spent many days in the garden watching thousands of ants crawling up the trunk of my prize peach tree.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. DCBA.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• D must open the paragraph as it introduces the subject for the first time — "my prize peach tree" — while watching ants crawl up its trunk.

• C follows D by describing this same tree in more detail — "The tree had grown against a warm wall on a sheltered side of the house" — continuing the description begun in D.

• B follows C, expressing the writer's feelings about the tree just described — "I am especially proud of it… it has survived several winters… produces luscious peaches" — the pronoun "it" refers back to "the tree" in C.

• A comes last, shifting to a new time reference ("During the summer") and a new development — the leaves beginning to wither — forming a natural continuation/contrast after the tree has been introduced and praised.
◦ Final order: D → C → B → A.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 (ABCD) is incorrect because it opens with A, whose reference to "the tree" ("the leaves of the tree") has no antecedent until D/C introduce the peach tree.

• Option 3 (CDBA) is incorrect because it opens with C, whose subject "The tree" has no prior introduction — D must come first to name the peach tree.

• Option 4 (BDAC) is incorrect because it opens with B, whose pronoun "it" has nothing to refer back to at the start of the paragraph.

NOTE

• In para-jumble questions, always find the sentence that introduces the subject/noun without a pronoun (here, D — "my prize peach tree") to identify the opening sentence.

• Track pronouns ("it", "this", "that") carefully — they must always refer to something already mentioned in an earlier sentence of the chosen order.

question:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in active voice.
Was the bag packed by Mary?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Did Mary pack the bag?

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The given sentence "Was the bag packed by Mary?" is an interrogative sentence in the Simple Past Tense, Passive Voice.

• Rule — Active Voice of Interrogative Sentences in Simple Past Tense:
◦ Passive: Was/Were + Object + V3 + by + Subject?
◦ Active: Did + Subject + V1 + Object?

• Applying the rule: the agent "Mary" becomes the subject; the auxiliary "Was" is replaced by "Did"; the past participle "packed" (V3) changes to its base form "pack" (V1); and "the bag" (the earlier subject) becomes the object.
◦ Active: Did Mary pack the bag?

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "Was Mary pack the bag?" wrongly retains the auxiliary "Was" with the base verb "pack", which is not a grammatically valid combination.

• Option 2: "Is Mary packing the bag?" incorrectly shifts the tense to the Present Continuous, changing the meaning of the original past-tense sentence.

• Option 3: "Do Mary pack the bag?" incorrectly uses "Do" (Present tense) with a third-person singular subject "Mary" (which needs "Does") and also changes the tense from past to present.

NOTE

• For Simple Past Tense questions in the active voice, always use the auxiliary "Did" followed by the base form (V1) of the verb, regardless of the subject's number/person.

• Do not confuse "Do/Does" (Simple Present) with "Did" (Simple Past) when converting voice.

question:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the word 'Optimistic' from the given sentence.
After the incident, Radha prepared herself to stay positive even in gloomy days.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. gloomy.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The word "Optimistic" means hopeful and confident about the future; having a positive outlook.

• Among the words present in the sentence, "gloomy" — meaning dark, dismal, and full of sadness or despair — is the closest in sense to the opposite of "optimistic" (a hopeful, positive outlook).
◦ Example: Despite the gloomy forecast, she remained optimistic about the team's chances.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "stay" is a verb meaning "to remain"; it carries no meaning opposite to "optimistic".

• Option 2: "incident" simply means an event or occurrence; it has no meaning-relationship with "optimistic".

• Option 3: "positive" is essentially a synonym, not an antonym, of "optimistic" — both describe a hopeful attitude.

NOTE

• Other antonyms of "optimistic": pessimistic, hopeless, despondent, cynical.

• Other synonyms of "optimistic": hopeful, positive, confident, sanguine.

question:
The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them may contain an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. If you don't find any error, mark 'No error' as your answer.
After knowing truth, / the jury took the right decision / in the case.
option_1: The jury took the right decision
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. After knowing truth.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The error lies in the phrase "After knowing truth"; the noun "truth", when it refers to a specific, particular truth (the truth of this case), must take the definite article "the" before it.

• Rule — Use of "the" with abstract nouns: Abstract nouns like "truth", "beauty", "honesty" are normally used without an article when speaking in a general sense, but they DO take "the" when they refer to something specific or particular, as understood from the context.
◦ Correct: After knowing the truth, the jury took the right decision in the case.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "the jury took the right decision" is grammatically correct — the collective noun "jury" is used with the singular verb "took" appropriately.

• Option 2: "in the case" is grammatically correct as it is, with the definite article correctly used before the specific noun "case".

• Option 4: "No error" is incorrect because the sentence does contain a grammatical error, as explained above, in the first part.

NOTE

• Abstract nouns take "the" when a particular instance is meant: compare "Honesty is the best policy" (general) with "I admired the honesty of his confession" (particular/specific).

• This is a commonly tested "missing article" error in SSC error-spotting questions.

question:
In the following sentence, four words are underlined, out of which one word is incorrectly spelt. Identify the INCORRECTLY spelt word.
A lot of spontanity is required from the speaker in an extempore speech. The speaker is expected to brainstorm ideas and give speech instantaneously.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. spontanity.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The word "spontanity" is spelt incorrectly; the correct spelling is "spontaneity" — the quality of being spontaneous, i.e. done or occurring naturally and without planning.
◦ Example: The comedian's act relied heavily on spontaneity and quick wit.

• Spelling key: SPONTAN + EITY, i.e. SPONT-A-N-E-I-T-Y. Note the "e" before "i" in the ending "-eity", which is often mistakenly dropped, producing the wrong form "spontanity".

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "instantaneously" is correctly spelt, meaning "occurring or done immediately, without delay".

• Option 2: "extempore" is correctly spelt, meaning "spoken or done without preparation".

• Option 3: "brainstorm" is correctly spelt, meaning "to think intensively, often in a group, to generate ideas".

NOTE

• The related adjective is "spontaneous"; note it also carries the "e" before "ous" — S-P-O-N-T-A-N-E-O-U-S.

• Other commonly misspelt "-eity"/"-iety" words in SSC: anxiety, variety, society, sobriety, spontaneity.

question:
Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words.
A person who believes that laws and governments are not necessary.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Anarchist.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• An "Anarchist" is a person who believes that laws and governments are not necessary and should be abolished, favouring a society based on voluntary cooperation. (अराजकतावादी — जो मानता है कि कानून और सरकार आवश्यक नहीं हैं)
◦ Example: The anarchist argued that all forms of imposed government authority should be dismantled.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "Antagonist" (विरोधी पात्र): A person who is actively opposed to someone or something, or the chief opponent of the protagonist in a story — unrelated to beliefs about government.

• Option 2: "Antichrist" (मसीह-विरोधी): A figure in Christian theology who opposes Christ; unrelated to political/anarchist belief.

• Option 4: "Adversary" (प्रतिद्वंद्वी): An opponent or enemy in a conflict or contest; a general term unrelated specifically to a belief about laws/government.

NOTE

• Similar one-word substitutes often tested: "Atheist" (one who does not believe in God), "Agnostic" (one who believes existence of God cannot be known), "Autocrat" (a ruler with absolute power).

• Do not confuse "Anarchist" (opposes government/law) with "Anachronist" (someone/something out of its correct time period).

question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.
Miss the boat
option_3: Missing good moments of your life
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Missing a good opportunity.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom "Miss the boat" means to lose a chance or opportunity to do or have something, usually because one acted too slowly or hesitated. (अच्छा अवसर गंवाना)
◦ Example: If you don't apply today, you will miss the boat for this scholarship.

• The idiom likely comes from literally missing a boat's scheduled departure because one arrived too late, extended metaphorically to any lost opportunity.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2: "Missing your medium of travel" is only the literal sense of the words and not the idiomatic/figurative meaning tested here.

• Option 3: "Missing good moments of your life" is a distortion of the idiom's meaning; the idiom is specifically about a lost chance/opportunity, not general good moments.

• Option 4: "Being too late" describes only the cause/manner of missing the boat, not the complete idiomatic meaning, which centres on the lost opportunity itself.

NOTE

• Other idioms about missed/lost chances often asked in SSC: "Cry over spilt milk" (to regret something that cannot be undone), "A day late and a dollar short", "Once in a blue moon" (a rare opportunity).

• Contrast with "Catch the bus/boat", meaning to seize an opportunity in time.

question:
Sentences of a paragraph are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the sentences in the correct order to form a meaningful and coherent paragraph.
(A) The outcome is much more likely to be favourable if there is substantial international aid than if there is not.
(B) Many of the underdeveloped countries will promote the growth of their economies in one way or the other, no matter whether they receive substantial outside aid in the process or not.
(C) By substantial aid I mean not only large amounts of technical assistance but also of capital.
(D) The character of that development, however, is likely to be strongly influenced by the types of and amounts of aid available.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. BDAC.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• B must open the paragraph as it introduces the main subject — that underdeveloped countries will promote economic growth regardless of outside aid.

• D follows B, picking up the phrase "that development", which refers directly back to the "growth of their economies" mentioned in B, and adds that its character is influenced by the type/amount of aid.

• A follows D, continuing the idea of aid's influence by stating that the outcome is more favourable with substantial aid — linking to "types of and amounts of aid" in D.

• C comes last, explaining/defining the key term "substantial aid" used in A ("By substantial aid I mean…"), which is a typical concluding clarification.
◦ Final order: B → D → A → C.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 (ABDC) is incorrect because it opens with A, whose phrase "if there is substantial international aid" presupposes a concept (aid affecting outcomes) not yet introduced.

• Option 3 (DABC) is incorrect because it opens with D, whose phrase "that development" has no antecedent without B coming first.

• Option 4 (DBCA) is incorrect because it opens with D for the same reason, and additionally places C (a definition of "substantial aid") before A, which uses that term without it being defined yet in a natural sequence.

NOTE

• Look for referring/back-pointing phrases like "that development" (D) and "By substantial aid I mean" (C) — these must follow the sentence that first introduces the term they refer to.

• The sentence that introduces a concept in general terms (here, B) almost always precedes the sentence that elaborates or narrows it (here, D, A, C).

question:
**In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

The Sun is the star at the center of (1)__________ Solar System. It is a nearly perfect ball of hot plasma. The Sun has inspired us since ancient times. It's central to mythology and religion in (2)_____________ around the world. It keeps our planet warm enough for living things to grow. It gives us light so we can see. It is by far the most important (3)__________of energy for life on Earth. It is about a hundred times as wide (4)_________ the Earth. If there were no sun, many things wouldn't occur like photosynthesis or the presence of oxygen, which would have caused no (5)__________ of life.**

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 1.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. the.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The blank requires the definite article "the" before "Solar System", since "Solar System" refers to one particular, unique system (our own) that is already known/specific to both writer and reader.

• Rule — Use of "the": The definite article "the" is used before nouns that denote something unique or one of a kind, such as the Sun, the Earth, the Solar System, the sky.
◦ Correct: The Sun is the star at the center of the Solar System.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "typical" is an adjective meaning "usual/representative"; it does not fit grammatically or logically before "Solar System" in this context.

• Option 2: "huge" is an adjective meaning "very large"; while descriptive, it is not the word required to complete the standard phrase "the Solar System", and using it without an article would still be ungrammatical.

• Option 4: "a" (indefinite article) is incorrect because "Solar System" here refers to the one specific, unique solar system we belong to, not any one of several — so "a" is grammatically wrong.

NOTE

• Other unique nouns that always take "the": the moon, the universe, the equator, the sky, the world.

• Distinguish "a/an" (used for a non-specific, one-of-many item) from "the" (used for a specific/unique item known to both speaker and listener).

question:
**In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

The Sun is the star at the center of (1)__________ Solar System. It is a nearly perfect ball of hot plasma. The Sun has inspired us since ancient times. It's central to mythology and religion in (2)_____________ around the world. It keeps our planet warm enough for living things to grow. It gives us light so we can see. It is by far the most important (3)__________of energy for life on Earth. It is about a hundred times as wide (4)_________ the Earth. If there were no sun, many things wouldn't occur like photosynthesis or the presence of oxygen, which would have caused no (5)__________ of life.**

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 2.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. cultures.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The blank requires a noun describing groups of people/civilisations found around the world; "cultures" fits naturally in the phrase "central to mythology and religion in cultures around the world", meaning the Sun holds importance in the mythology and religion of various cultures across the globe.
◦ Example: The Sun god appears in the mythology and religion of many ancient cultures around the world, from Egypt to the Americas.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2: "processes" refers to a series of actions/steps; it does not fit the context of mythology and religion belonging to groups of people.

• Option 3: "scenes" refers to a place/setting of an event or a view; it is not a logical fit for "mythology and religion in ___ around the world".

• Option 4: "types" refers to categories/kinds; it is too vague and does not correctly complete the intended meaning of mythology/religion being found across different human cultures.

NOTE

• The passage is describing the Sun's role in human mythology across different civilisations; "culture" (a people's shared customs, beliefs, and practices) is the standard word used in such a context.

• This is a reading-comprehension/cloze vocabulary-in-context question — always re-read the full sentence to check which option makes complete logical sense, not just grammatical sense.

question:
**In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

The Sun is the star at the center of (1)__________ Solar System. It is a nearly perfect ball of hot plasma. The Sun has inspired us since ancient times. It's central to mythology and religion in (2)_____________ around the world. It keeps our planet warm enough for living things to grow. It gives us light so we can see. It is by far the most important (3)__________of energy for life on Earth. It is about a hundred times as wide (4)_________ the Earth. If there were no sun, many things wouldn't occur like photosynthesis or the presence of oxygen, which would have caused no (5)__________ of life.**

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 3.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. source.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The blank requires a noun completing the phrase **"the most important ___ of energy"; "source" is the standard collocation used for something that provides or originates energy.
◦ Example:** The Sun is the primary source of energy for almost all life on Earth.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "gesture" means a movement of the body/hands to express meaning; it is unrelated to the concept of energy.

• Option 3: "control" means the power to influence/direct something; it does not fit the phrase "the most important ___ of energy".

• Option 4: "symbol" means a sign/mark representing something else; while the Sun can be called a symbol in other contexts, "symbol of energy" does not fit the meaning intended here (that the Sun provides/originates energy for life).

NOTE

• The fixed collocation "source of energy" is very commonly tested in SSC cloze passages — remember other similar collocations: "source of income", "source of information", "source of light".

question:
**In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

The Sun is the star at the center of (1)__________ Solar System. It is a nearly perfect ball of hot plasma. The Sun has inspired us since ancient times. It's central to mythology and religion in (2)_____________ around the world. It keeps our planet warm enough for living things to grow. It gives us light so we can see. It is by far the most important (3)__________of energy for life on Earth. It is about a hundred times as wide (4)_________ the Earth. If there were no sun, many things wouldn't occur like photosynthesis or the presence of oxygen, which would have caused no (5)__________ of life.**

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 4.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. as.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The blank completes a comparative structure of equality: "as + adjective/adverb + as" — here, "as wide as the Earth".

• Rule — Comparison of Equality: To compare two things that are equal in some quality, English uses the structure "as + adjective + as" (e.g., "as tall as", "as wide as", "as fast as").
◦ Correct: It is about a hundred times as wide as the Earth.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "about" does not fit the required comparative structure "as ___ as" and would create an ungrammatical sentence if inserted here.

• Option 3: "like" used in the form "wide like the Earth" is not standard English for expressing this multiple/proportional comparison, and it breaks the required "as…as" pattern.

• Option 4: "than" is used with comparative adjectives (e.g. "wider than"), not with the positive form "wide"; using "than" after "wide" (not "wider") is grammatically incorrect.

NOTE

• Do not confuse the comparison of equality ("as…as", for equal degree) with the comparison of superiority ("…er than" / "more…than", for unequal degree).

• Common exam trap: "as wide as" (correct) vs "wider than" (also correct in its own structure) — but never mix the two forms, e.g. "as wider than" is wrong.

question:
**In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

The Sun is the star at the center of (1)__________ Solar System. It is a nearly perfect ball of hot plasma. The Sun has inspired us since ancient times. It's central to mythology and religion in (2)_____________ around the world. It keeps our planet warm enough for living things to grow. It gives us light so we can see. It is by far the most important (3)__________of energy for life on Earth. It is about a hundred times as wide (4)_________ the Earth. If there were no sun, many things wouldn't occur like photosynthesis or the presence of oxygen, which would have caused no (5)__________ of life.**

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 5.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. existence.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The blank completes the phrase **"caused no ___ of life", meaning that without the Sun (and hence no photosynthesis or oxygen), there would be no existence of life on Earth at all.
◦ Example:** Without sunlight, there would be no existence of plant life on our planet.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "skill" means an ability to do something well; it does not logically fit "no ___ of life".

• Option 2: "end" means a finish/conclusion; "caused no end of life" would suggest life never finishes, which contradicts the passage's meaning that there would be no life at all.

• Option 3: "enhancement" means an improvement; "no enhancement of life" would mean life is not improved, not that life fails to exist at all, which is a weaker and less precise fit than "existence".

NOTE

• The passage builds a cause-effect chain: no sun → no photosynthesis/oxygen → no existence of life; the final blank must logically complete this chain with the strongest, most complete outcome — the total absence of life ("existence"), not a partial idea like "no end" or "no enhancement".

• In cloze passages, always check the overall logical flow/argument of the paragraph, not just grammar, when multiple options are grammatically valid.
